claim: Synthetic review exercises, not model evaluation or reproduced exploits.

target_bindings.actors: Two callers allowed to enqueue jobs.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Read capacity, wait for remote validation, then insert job.
target_bindings.delivery: Validation completions can arrive in either order.
target_bindings.authority: Each caller may reserve only capacity allowed by its quota.
target_bindings.recovery: Failed validation must release only that request's reservation.

cases.candidate: Both callers pass the capacity read, then both insert after validation.
cases.safe_control: A conditional insert reserves a slot in a serializable transaction before validation; completion uses a unique reservation ID.
cases.expected: Investigate the first schedule; exclude the control only after proving its isolation and reservation semantics.
cases.renaming_control: Rename enqueue to allocate_session and jobs to sessions without changing behavior; applicability must remain the same.

target_bindings.actors: Customer, merchant service, external payment processor.
target_bindings.resource: One charge and its merchant ledger entry.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Processor charge commits separately from the merchant database update.
target_bindings.delivery: Timeout can occur after a successful charge; jobs may be redelivered.
target_bindings.authority: The customer's authorization covers one logical payment.
target_bindings.recovery: Query the charge by immutable idempotency key before another attempt.

cases.candidate: A timeout is treated as proof of failure; retry creates a second charge and increments customer spending twice.
cases.safe_control: The processor enforces one charge per logical payment key; the merchant reconciles outcome and records the ledger entry idempotently.
cases.expected: Trace actual committed charges, ambiguous acknowledgements, and counter commits. Do not infer the charge failed from the timeout.
cases.renaming_control: An API named mint_receipt that only records a log is not an external value-creation effect; names do not establish prerequisites.

target_bindings.actors: Migration operator and normal account writers.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Snapshot, copied pages, and cutover are separate commits.
target_bindings.delivery: A worker may retry or another migration may start.
target_bindings.authority: Only operators migrate; ordinary users can still transfer entitlements.
target_bindings.recovery: Checkpoint pages and replay a complete ordered change log.

cases.candidate: The copy uses an old snapshot while writes continue and a second operator can start the same migration.
cases.safe_control: A unique migration epoch prevents overlap; a consistent snapshot plus exact-once change capture includes intervening writes before cutover.
cases.expected: Treat operator overlap and intervening user writes as distinct causes. A pause is one possible control, not the only safe architecture.
cases.renaming_control: Using a document store instead of SQL does not remove the mechanism if the same boundaries remain.

target_bindings.resource: Inventory reservation, order attempts, dispatch command.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Local order deletion does not remove an already-delivered warehouse command.
target_bindings.delivery: Replacement and original commands may both remain executable.
target_bindings.authority: A warehouse command authorizes dispatch to its bound recipient.
target_bindings.recovery: Reconcile dispatch status before releasing stock and admission markers.

cases.candidate: Cancel deletes the order but retains its consumed request key and an executable dispatch command.
cases.safe_control: Cancellation is disallowed after irreversible dispatch; earlier cancellation atomically preserves a recoverable claim and reconciles the request key.
cases.expected: Separate the surviving authority from blocked recovery. An immutable rightful recipient does not alone establish theft.
cases.renaming_control: A method named revoke that only deletes a row is not evidence of external revocation.

target_bindings.commit_boundary: Upload parsing commits before signature verification and malware screening.
target_bindings.delivery: Screening completion is deferred and can fail.
target_bindings.authority: Only approved publisher artifacts may deploy.
target_bindings.recovery: Release provisional capacity and quarantine unapproved artifacts.

cases.candidate: Readable metadata is enough to reserve all deployment capacity and mark an unverified artifact ready.
cases.safe_control: Capacity is bounded and provisional, readiness requires all actual validators, and failure safely releases the reservation.
cases.expected: Verify actual integrity policy, validator rejection, readiness predicates, shared-resource impact, and recovery.
cases.renaming_control: This service has no chain maturity or proof circuit; only its own signature and screening rules apply.

target_bindings.actors: Account holder, batch service, destination provider.
target_bindings.resource: Customer funds, provider costs, partial acceptance, and residual credit.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Each destination payout can settle independently.
target_bindings.delivery: A batch response reports accepted amounts, not unused amounts.
target_bindings.authority: Residual credit belongs to the original account holder.
target_bindings.recovery: Retain below-minimum and rejected amounts in a withdrawable customer balance.

cases.candidate: Any positive accepted amount is treated as full settlement and an unusable post-fee remainder disappears.
cases.safe_control: The service reconciles accepted amount, costs, and customer remainder, validates provider-specific minima, and preserves feasible recovery.
cases.expected: Use the actual accepted/unused polarity and downstream policy. Do not invent partial acceptance for an enforced atomic all-or-nothing provider.
cases.renaming_control: Identical 'success' fields in two providers can mean different business outcomes; bind each interface.

target_bindings.actors: Tenant creating versions and storage billing service.
target_bindings.resource: Bytes replicated into versions and indexes.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Each copy persists separately from billing.
target_bindings.delivery: Copy operations can retry and create retained versions.
target_bindings.authority: Tenant pays marginal retained storage under current pricing.
target_bindings.recovery: Delete versions and reconcile charges and credits.

cases.candidate: New objects are priced correctly, but copying large legacy objects repeats an uncharged embedded attachment.
cases.safe_control: All actual byte deltas are charged, or a documented bounded legacy subsidy funds the copies.
cases.expected: Measure old/new and short/long controls, payer cost, retained copies, and cleanup before asserting resource harm.
cases.renaming_control: Memory, storage, and bandwidth have distinct cost models even if all are called size.

target_bindings.actors: End user, forwarding client, scoped API key, external processor.
target_bindings.resource: Original payment account and refund recipient.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: A request remains pending while processor configuration changes.
target_bindings.delivery: Old-generation responses may arrive after rotation.
target_bindings.authority: Key scopes, original user, immediate caller, and payer are distinct.
target_bindings.recovery: Refund the original payer through the original funded account under explicit revocation policy.

cases.candidate: A delayed refund reads the new global account and pays the request originator instead of the actual payer.
cases.safe_control: Immutable request context binds resource generation and payer; response acceptance follows explicit generation policy and credential scopes.
cases.expected: Prove forwarding, rotation, and limited-credential reachability. The appropriate controls are target-specific capabilities, not a universal attached-payment guard.
cases.renaming_control: Do not infer authority solely from variables named owner, signer, or caller.

target_bindings.resource: One locally allocated record and its accounting row.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: Both writes occur in one serializable transaction; no external side effects.
target_bindings.delivery: Failed transactions roll back all writes.
target_bindings.authority: Clients may allocate only when capacity is available.
target_bindings.recovery: Retry the entire transaction after rollback.

cases.candidate: A reviewer assumes a gap because the source has a check followed by two writes.
cases.safe_control: The database demonstrably enforces serializable execution and atomic rollback for all these effects.
cases.expected: Not applicable to these mechanisms under the established semantics; do not manufacture independent commits from sequential source lines.
cases.renaming_control: Renaming the two writes to mint and finalize does not create separate commit boundaries.

target_bindings.resource: Expense approval and optional category restrictions.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: A request becomes executable after a configured review period.
target_bindings.delivery: Notifications are asynchronous; review is an explicit trust assumption.
target_bindings.authority: Membership grants eligibility; category rules only restrict it.
target_bindings.recovery: Reviewer can veto before execution; disabling configuration is independently verified.

cases.candidate: A reviewer calls absent category restrictions and no-veto execution authorization bugs.
cases.safe_control: Documented policy intentionally permits unrestricted members and optimistic approval; implementation matches those rules.
cases.expected: Do not report those intended semantics as a bypass. Investigate only a demonstrated mismatch, hidden prerequisite, or promised availability failure.
cases.renaming_control: A setting called whitelist can be restrictive or permissive; the name alone does not establish policy.

target_bindings.actors: Worker, retry scheduler, operator resizing history.
target_bindings.resource: Leased capacity, deduplication history, and cancellation attempts.
target_bindings.commit_boundary: History, completion, and cancellation are separately persisted.
target_bindings.delivery: Completion evidence can arrive after a lease deadline.
target_bindings.authority: Worker leases permit execution only within their validity rules.
target_bindings.recovery: Reconcile timely completed work before releasing capacity, and retry a failed cancellation.

cases.candidate: A resize forgets relevant completed work and an expired cancellation leaves a reservation without retry.
cases.safe_control: History epochs survive resize, recovery is idempotent, and evidence is checked against execution time rather than observation time.
cases.expected: Prove actual eviction and expiry semantics. Passage of time does not universally revoke authority or remove history.
cases.renaming_control: Timeout, expiry, and retention are different concepts even when represented by timestamps.
